overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's essays on painting. You'll be asked about lived perspective, Cézanne's project, the painter's body in "Eye and Mind," the critique of Descartes's optics, and painting as expression.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: In a Cézanne still life, a tabletop tilts toward the viewer more than geometric perspective allows. How does Merleau-Ponty interpret this?

options.html: As a technical error Cézanne never corrected
options.text: As a technical error Cézanne never corrected
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty argues that the distortion isn't an error. It records lived perspective.

options.html: As a record of how the table appears to a moving eye
options.text: As a record of how the table appears to a moving eye
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The tilt tracks how the eye takes in the surface from successive positions, which is lived perspective.

options.html: As a symbol of Cézanne's anxious temperament
options.text: As a symbol of Cézanne's anxious temperament
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty rejects explaining the work by the life. The tilt records lived perspective.

options.html: As an early step toward purely abstract painting
options.text: As an early step toward purely abstract painting
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Cézanne wanted to return to the object. The tilt records how the table is lived.

forms.stemHtml: What did Cézanne try to paint, according to Merleau-Ponty?

options.html: The play of light on surfaces, as the Impressionists did
options.text: The play of light on surfaces, as the Impressionists did
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Cézanne thought Impressionism dissolved objects into light. He wanted primordial perception.

options.html: Objects composed by rules of outline and perspective
options.text: Objects composed by rules of outline and perspective
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Cézanne refused academic composition as well. He wanted primordial perception.

options.html: The world as it takes form in perception, before thought
options.text: The world as it takes form in perception, before thought
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty calls this primordial perception: the object in the act of appearing.

options.html: Private feelings projected onto a neutral landscape
options.text: Private feelings projected onto a neutral landscape
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Cézanne's project concerns perception, not the projection of feeling. He wanted primordial perception.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following does Merleau-Ponty argue in "Eye and Mind"? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The painter paints by lending a body to the world
options.text: The painter paints by lending a body to the world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty borrows Valéry's remark that the painter takes his body along.

options.html: The body that sees is itself visible, a thing among things
options.text: The body that sees is itself visible, a thing among things
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the enigma of the body: the seer is also seen.

options.html: Descartes's account of vision loses color, depth, and the body
options.text: Descartes's account of vision loses color, depth, and the body
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Modeled on engravings, it reduces seeing to the mind reading signs.

options.html: Painting should copy the scene as exactly as a photograph
options.text: Painting should copy the scene as exactly as a photograph
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty holds that painting makes seeing visible. It doesn't copy.

options.html: Science should be abandoned in favor of art
options.text: Science should be abandoned in favor of art
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. He criticizes operational thought for forgetting the perceived world, not science itself.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's name for scientific thinking that manipulates things through models and treats everything as an object in general, without inhabiting it? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! "Eye and Mind" opens with this diagnosis of science.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty calls this operational thought.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty say Cézanne's doubt belongs to expression itself, not only to Cézanne?

options.html: Because every painter has an anxious temperament
options.text: Because every painter has an anxious temperament
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The doubt isn't psychological. It comes from expression having no finished meaning to copy.

options.html: Because painting can never represent objects at all
options.text: Because painting can never represent objects at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Painting can render objects. The point is that its meaning isn't settled in advance.

options.html: Because critics judged Cézanne's work too harshly
options.text: Because critics judged Cézanne's work too harshly
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The doubt isn't about critics. It comes from the risk built into expression.

options.html: Because a work's meaning isn't available before it's made
options.text: Because a work's meaning isn't available before it's made
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With no finished meaning to check against, all expression runs this risk.

title: Painting and Vision
